newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices up again on US heating oil demand, Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices up again on US heating oil demand, Iraq.

text.p: World oil prices headed higher again on Thursday, helped up by increased U.S. heating oil demand and reports of instability in Iraq.

Analysts said the general upturn was still a continuation of the bounce off Monday's four-month lows, but increased heating oil demand and reports on Iraq gave the market an excuse to push higher as well.
White House press secretary Mike McCurry said on Wednesday there were "a great deal of complicated internal struggles for power" going on inside Iraq.
London March futures for international benchmark crude oil Brent closed up 40 cents at $23.17 a barrel, having reached a session high of $23.00
"I think it's a follow-through from yesterday and gas oil (heating oil) has moved higher to catch up with what happened on Brent," said Charles Gray, an energy analyst at Prudential Bache in London.

Oil markets took little notice of Thursday's announcement by United Nations (U.N.) Secretary General Kofi Annan that he expected the oil-for-food deal with Iraq to be renewed in June for another six months.
Under a U.N. agreement Iraq is permitted to sell $2 billion worth of crude oil over six months to pay for humanitarian supplies.

Some analysts said the rise was a seasonal pattern influenced by colder weather forecasts and American Petroleum Institute (API) data released on Tuesday, which showed distillate stocks, including heating oil fell further than the market had expected.

"The market continues primarily to be thinking in terms of supply and demand and right now they're worried that demand has been picking up at a time when supply is potentially a bit vulnerable," Gray said.
Independent forecaster Weather Services Corporation saw below average temperatures for the U.S. Northeast, the world's largest heating oil market, over the next few days.
They said this was likely to result in increased heating oil needs.
